results.content:
The absence of staining, buckling, odor, or transfer is reassuring, but ordinary cardboard should not remain in contact with the watercolor. It can be acidic, lignin-containing, and chemically unstable, allowing acids or discoloration to migrate into the paper over time.

Most conservative approach

1. Leave the watercolor undisturbed until you can work on a clean, dry table.
2. Photograph both sides and the frame package before changing anything.
3. Remove the ordinary cardboard only if it lifts freely. Do not pull if the sheet is stuck, tacky, or catches.
4. Replace the contact surface with a conservation-grade package rather than simply inserting a random sheet of paper.

Suitable materials

- 100% cotton-rag mat board, or chemically purified lignin-free board, preferably 4-ply or thicker.
- Acid-free, lignin-free corrugated board at least about 3 mm thick for structural backing.
- A polyester or metalized-polyester moisture barrier behind the archival backing board, not directly against friable paint.
- Conservation-grade, acid-free interleaving tissue for temporary protection. Use unbuffered tissue if it will touch the artwork, and do not use it if the paint is powdery, flaking, or easily transferred.
- A conservation mat or spacer so the watercolor cannot touch the glazing.
- Reversible, non-adhesive mounting where possible: photo corners, mounting strips, or a professionally made Japanese-tissue-and-wheat-starch hinge system.

Avoid

- Ordinary cardboard, kraft paper, newspaper, paper towels, and unknown “acid-free” craft board.
- Pressure-sensitive tape, masking tape, double-sided tape, glue, spray adhesive, laminating film, or self-adhesive plastic.
- Plastic wrap or an airtight improvised enclosure, which can trap moisture.
- Foam board unless the framer can identify it as conservation-grade and chemically stable.
- Polyester film directly over the painted face, especially if the medium is friable; static can lift loose pigment.
- Pressing, burnishing, ironing, or flattening the sheet yourself.

Practical options

Option 1: Temporary isolation

If the sheet separates cleanly and the paint is stable, place it face-up on a clean, inert surface and use a single sheet of clean conservation tissue as a temporary interleaf over it. Keep the package flat, dry, and loosely protected from dust while arranging proper reframing. Do not tape the tissue to the artwork or seal the edges.

This is a holding measure, not a finished framing solution. Tissue should not be allowed to rub against a loose or textured paint surface during repeated handling.

Option 2: Replace the backing in the existing frame

Ask a conservation-oriented framer to replace the ordinary cardboard with a proper archival back mat and structural backing. The framer should:

- Keep the sheet off the backing through reversible mounting or a designed mat system.
- Leave enough room for normal paper movement.
- Add a spacer or window mat so the artwork does not touch the glazing.
- Use a moisture barrier and stable backing.
- Secure the package with pins, brads, or an appropriate frame-fitting method rather than taping the artwork or package together with pressure-sensitive tape.

For this 7-by-9-inch watercolor, a simple archival window mat is usually the least complicated protective solution. If preserving all edges and showing the sheet floating is important, request a reversible float mount or sink mount rather than an adhesive-mounted presentation. Since your earlier framing treatment used a full-sheet archival float mount and UV-filtering acrylic, you could ask the framer whether that same type of package can be restored or adapted here.

Option 3: Have the whole package rebuilt

This is preferable if the current frame has no proper spacer, the backing is warped, the sheet is unsupported, or the artwork has been placed directly against the cardboard for a long time. Specify:

- 100% cotton-rag mat or back mat
- Reversible mounting
- UV-filtering glazing
- No contact between watercolor and glazing
- Stable backing plus moisture barrier
- No pressure-sensitive adhesive on the artwork

UV-filtering glazing reduces light damage but does not make direct sun safe and does not solve contact with acidic cardboard.

Handling precautions

- Wash and thoroughly dry your hands; handle the sheet by its edges with full support underneath.
- Keep food, drinks, water jars, and cleaning sprays away from the work surface.
- Do not stack anything on the watercolor.
- Do not flex the sheet to test it.
- Work under even light and inspect both sides without rubbing.
- If there is a mat or mount already attached, do not try to peel it away.
- Keep the frame out of direct sun, radiators, vents, kitchens, bathrooms, exterior damp walls, attics, and basements.

Involve a professional framer if:

- The cardboard is easy to remove and the artwork is otherwise clean, flat, stable, and undamaged.
- You mainly need an archival mat, backing, spacer, and proper frame assembly.
- You want to preserve the full sheet or use a float mount without improvising an adhesive attachment.

Involve a paper conservator rather than only a framer if:

- The sheet is stuck to the cardboard or lifts fibers when separated.
- There is mold, a musty odor, staining, tide lines, foxing, or suspected insect damage.
- The paper is cockled, brittle, torn, delaminating, or severely discolored.
- Pigment is flaking, powdery, tacky, or transfers to tissue.
- There is pressure-sensitive tape, glue, spray adhesive, or an unknown prior repair.
- The artwork has significant sentimental, financial, or exhibition value and you want a condition assessment before changing the package.

The Library of Congress gives similar guidance: use chemically stable mat and backing materials, 100% cotton rag or lignin-free board, reversible hinging where possible, a moisture barrier, and glazing that is separated from the object. Its framing guidance is here:

https://www.loc.gov/preservation/care/mat.html

results.content:
Because the wash is intact and the sheet is not torn through, treat this as a small surface-fiber lift—not a painting or structural repair. My conservative recommendation is to stabilize it dry, mock up the mat, and defer paste unless the edge proves unstable.

1. Document and inspect

- Photograph the front and back before touching it.
- Leave the sheet completely dry.
- Examine the lower edge in raking light. Determine whether the fibers are merely fuzzy/raised or whether a flap actually moves independently.
- Do not pull, rub, erase, sand, wet, or trim attached fibers. If a completely detached whisker is catching, trim only its free tip with very sharp scissors; otherwise leave it.

2. Set down only fibers that are already raised

If the lift is attached but standing proud:

- Put a smooth release surface—glassine or other clean, non-shedding release paper—over the damaged strip.
- Apply one brief, very light, even pressure with a clean flat object. Do not rub or burnish.
- If you do not have a suitable smooth release paper, skip this step rather than placing blotter directly against the fibers; blotter can catch on a rough edge.

Then leave it flat and undisturbed. Use the clean blotter only as an outer protective layer, not directly against the lifted fibers.

3. Make a reversible mat mock-up

Before repairing, place the painting in the intended mat without adhesive and check it at normal viewing distance and under oblique light.

The safest outcome is:

- a conservation-quality, lignin-free 4-ply or heavier window mat and back mat;
- an opening that completely covers the damaged lower strip without crowding or pinching the edge;
- an air space between the watercolor and glazing;
- no pressure-sensitive tape or adhesive touching the lower edge.

For mounting, use nonadhesive corners, edge strips, or another method that allows the sheet to move slightly. If hinges are necessary, they should normally be lightweight Japanese tissue hinges attached to the verso and back mat—not to the window mat—and not placed across the damaged edge. The Library of Congress and Canadian Conservation Institute both identify nonadhesive attachments or reversible wheat-starch hinges as preferable to tape.

4. Decide based on stability, not perfection

Leave it under the mat if:

- the fibers do not move during careful handling;
- the edge does not catch on the interleaf or mat;
- the damage is fully outside the window opening; and
- it is not conspicuous at normal viewing distance.

That is a legitimate conservation choice here. A mat can protect and conceal minor edge damage without altering the painting.

Consider repair only if:

- a flap is lifting or separating;
- fibers continue to shed;
- the edge catches during matting or handling; or
- the damage remains visible inside the opening.

I would not use the original offcut and wheat-starch paste as an improvised patch at this stage. A paper patch can be stiffer than the sheet and may create a ridge, and the moisture from paste can distort paper or migrate toward the watercolor. Preserve the offcut as a reference or future repair material. If repair becomes necessary, a paper conservator would normally use a very thin, long-fiber Japanese tissue on the verso with a controlled amount of paste, followed by restrained drying.

Do not put paste, sizing, matte medium, or fresh watercolor on the front. Given the facts you supplied, I would stabilize dry, test the mat, and leave it unrepaired if the mat fully protects and conceals the strip.

References:

https://www.loc.gov/preservation/care/mat.html

https://canada.ca/en/conservation-institute/services/conservation-preservation-publications/canadian-conservation-institute-notes/matting-works-paper.html

https://guides.loc.gov/matting-hinging-art-on-paper/mounting-and-hinging/paper-hinges

input.title: Historical design card — approved 2026 Helio Start paid-search pilot
input.body:
Historical design card

Program: Helio Start
Decision status: Approved pilot design; historical record as of 2028-01-01
Original launch: April 15, 2026, 9:00–9:30 AM Central

Acquisition type
- High-intent paid-search acquisition only.
- No broader paid-acquisition or unsupported expansion was implied.
- Paid source did not bypass existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, admission, lifecycle, instrumentation, support-routing, or suppression rules.

Duration
- Maximum duration: six weeks.
- Scheduled/live window: April 15 through May 26, 2026 at the latest.
- The pilot closed earlier if any controlling stop, pause, spend cap, or admission cap applied.

Budget and closure cap
- Maximum budget: $15,000 in spend.
- Close at the earlier of:
  - $15,000 in spend;
  - 50 admitted workspaces; or
  - the six-week limit, ending no later than May 26, 2026.
- At cap close, paid-search campaigns, ad groups, budgets, and associated paid landing/routing paths were to be paused immediately; no admissions were to be extended beyond the 50-workspace cohort.
- No pipeline target or forecast credit.

Launch gate
- Paid traffic remained blocked until paid-source attribution reconciled from eligibility-flow start through admission and assisted routing/final route.
- Launch required the preflight reconciliation to pass for all 24 admitted, assisted-review, and ineligible cases.
- The final gate was cleared April 11, 2026: the paid-source defect was corrected, all 24 cases reconciled through their final routes, and lifecycle branches and suppression behavior were confirmed unchanged. Launch authorization was then set for April 15.

Stop and pause rules
- Stop immediately and hold/quarantine the pilot if any unsupported applicant entered the admitted path; escalate the exception rather than silently correcting it.
- Pause immediately if a routing or instrumentation failure prevented paid-source attribution or final-route reconciliation.
- After at least 20 admissions, pause for support-load review if more than 10% of admitted workspaces exceeded 90 account-level support minutes.
- Existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules remained controlling.

Measurement and complete outcome windows
- Day-7 first integration was a leading operating indicator only. Complete day-7 windows were required before interpreting downstream behavior.
- The following measures required complete outcome windows before any mature claim:
  - paid-active status;
  - refund-adjusted collected cash; and
  - mature account-level support effort.
- Early operating checks could report routing/reconciliation integrity, admissions, spend, and day-7 leading indicators, but could not support mature acquisition, revenue, pipeline, forecast, or scale conclusions without the required complete windows and denominators.

Design boundary
- This was a bounded, descriptive pilot—not authorization for an ongoing acquisition program. Any continuation or new paid test required a separate decision, budget approval, and mature outcome evidence.

input.title: Board-source QA case — Q2 source completeness vs claim readiness
input.body:
QA training case

Source: June 12 Q2 board-evidence source-completeness packet.

The QA distinction
Source completeness asks: “Are the required evidence fields present, owned, defined, bounded, and traceable?” Claim readiness asks: “Is the evidence mature and appropriate enough to support the proposed claim?” These are separate judgments. A section can be source-complete for preparation while still being unsuitable for a claim, or a source-complete record can explicitly preserve a maturity limitation.

What passed source-completeness review
- Expansion Assist
- Pricing-page path quality
- CS auto-nudge

For each, the packet reported the required source owner, denominator or exact coverage fields, measurement limits, exclusions, and reliability-evidence locations, with no required source field missing. “Passed” here means source-complete preparation; it does not mean a claim was approved or that the lane is board-ready.

The maturity-dependent exception: Helio Start
Helio Start was the exception because its mature customer-outcome row was not complete. The cohort was a fixed 50-workspace paid pilot. The packet could use the complete leading read: 39 of 50 workspaces reached first integration by day 7. However, all 50 workspaces did not yet have complete day-90 windows. Therefore, the mature outcome could not be treated as claim-ready.

Until complete day-90 windows exist, do not report Helio Start as paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, or account-level support effort. The day-7 result is a leading read only; it is not evidence for acquisition, growth, revenue, forecast, or other mature customer-outcome claims.

QA answer key
1. “All four lanes passed source completeness, so all four are claim-ready.” Incorrect. Source completeness and claim readiness are different judgments.
2. “Helio Start had no usable evidence.” Incorrect. It had a fixed 50-workspace paid cohort and a complete 39-of-50 day-7 first-integration read.
3. “The day-7 read proves the mature customer outcome.” Incorrect. The complete day-90 windows were still missing for the cohort.
4. Correct classification: three sections were source-complete preparation sections; Helio Start retained a maturity-dependent exception for its mature-outcome row.

Limits of the June 12 packet
The packet made no claim, closed no lane, and made no board-readiness decision. It documented source completeness and the Helio Start maturity boundary only. It did not approve executive wording, causal interpretation, revenue or forecast treatment, or a final board claim. Those decisions remained outside this packet.

results.content: Daniela and Owen finished the beta-only evidence-tier dry run on 30 held January Helio Start applicants. Eighteen exact-domain cases passed automatically, nine legitimate parent-company or IT-managed identities only passed once they had corroborating admin evidence, and three agency identities were routed to Customer Success instead of self-attestation. Every applicant row produced exactly one current entitlement state and one support state, with no blanks, duplicate workspace records, or merged states. I'm accepting that as the intake rule for the next controlled batch, but I'm not broadening exposure from here. Please create a January 18, 2024 calendar event from 2:00pm to 2:45pm Central for me, Priya, Daniela, Owen, Ines, and Customer Success. The notes should cover support load, admin proof, entitlement and support-state integrity, and the unsupported lifecycle list, and they need to say explicitly that this is a controlled-beta readiness gate rather than a GA, public signup, pricing-page, or paid-acquisition decision.

Helio Start readiness evidence

52 observed records
- Admin proof passed: 27/52
- Agency identities routed before setup: 3/52
- Activated by day 7: 14/52
- Had a support contact: 5/52

Recommendation: The combined evidence supports expanding Helio Start exposure.

Underlying sources:
- Intake dry run: 30 held applications — 18 exact-domain automatic passes, 9 parent-company or IT-managed passes after corroborating evidence, and 3 agency identities routed to Customer Success.
- Q4 outcome evidence: 22 accepted workspaces — 14 activated by day 7 and 5 had a support contact. Every workspace has one current entitlement state and one support state.

Daniela —

I like exact domain match as positive evidence, but I don’t think “match → verified, otherwise → route” is ready to become the rule. It risks treating a useful signal as a complete ownership determination and could misclassify legitimate cases, especially:

- Parent-company domains where the workspace operates under a subsidiary or business-unit identity
- IT-managed SSO, where the person authenticating may not own the customer domain
- Shared or delegated administration, where the relevant admin uses a different domain
- Existing agency or inherited-admin arrangements

I’d keep the November definition unchanged for comparability and treat this as a January readiness question, not a retroactive taxonomy change. The November rows should remain classified under the existing definition, with ambiguous ownership annotated rather than recoded.

For January, I’d separate the outcomes:

1. Automatic proof  
   Exact domain match can count as automatic proof when it matches the workspace’s established customer domain and there are no contradictory ownership or SSO signals.

2. Corroboration required  
   Parent-company domains, IT-managed SSO, shared aliases, delegated administration, agency involvement, or any conflicting identity/domain evidence should be marked as needing corroboration—not automatically routed or automatically accepted.

3. Assisted route  
   If corroboration cannot establish who controls the relevant admin access, route the account to the assisted path, consistent with the November boundary.

Before anyone discusses implementation, could you pull a small historical edge-case sample—perhaps 10–15 cases—with the observed domain relationship, SSO/admin context, eventual ownership outcome, and whether the account required assistance? I’d especially like a few parent-company and IT-managed SSO examples. That will tell us whether the proposed categories cover the real cases and whether exact domain match is strong enough to serve as automatic proof in the clean subset.

Thanks,  
Riley

Admin-ownership evidence tiers — January readiness question

- False-negative check: Assess whether strict matching would incorrectly exclude legitimate admins using parent-company domains, IT-managed SSO, shared aliases, or delegated administration.

These are January readiness questions to validate against the historical sample—not a November recode or an implementation decision.

Treat this as a duplicate-application reconciliation, not as a new application and not as a deletion of one intake row.

1. Count treatment

There are:

- 25 raw intake rows
- 24 unique applications
- 1 duplicate group containing 2 rows
- 23 unrelated applications

The cap denominator is the unique-application count: 24, not 25. The company represented by the waitlist row and referral row consumes one application slot. If these are the only applications in the cap scope, the remaining capacity is 96 of 120.

Keep the raw row count at 25 in the audit view. The operational application count should become 24. Do not hard-delete the duplicate intake row merely to make the count appear correct.

2. Contain the affected pair

Before changing either row:

- Pause processing for only these two matching rows.
- Do not pause the other 23 applications.
- Snapshot both intake rows and their child entitlement and support-state objects.
- Record the exact company domain, admin email, source channel, row IDs, creation timestamps, and the 17-minute interval.
- Confirm that neither row has an invitation event, workspace creation, or Customer Success route. The stated facts should be verified from the event tables, not inferred from the absence of a visible status field.

Use the exact stored identifiers for the audit. If comparison logic uses case folding or whitespace handling, retain the original domain and email values unchanged in the provenance record.

3. Canonical-record choice

Use the earlier waitlist row as the canonical application because it is the first valid intake record for the company. The later referral row becomes a linked duplicate or alias.

That choice is deterministic and avoids treating a later retry or referral as a second application. It should not be based on whichever row happens to have the lower database ID or whichever child object was created first.

The only reason to reverse that choice would be evidence that the referral row contains an authoritative, later correction to the application—not merely a repeated submission. If that occurs, record the exception and the approving owner rather than silently choosing the later row.

The canonical record should retain:

- Its original application ID
- Its original waitlist provenance
- A linked provenance entry for the referral row
- Both original timestamps
- Both source channels
- The duplicate relationship, for example:
  - `duplicate_group_id`
  - `canonical_application_id`
  - `duplicate_of`
  - `source_channel`
  - `source_row_id`
  - `linked_at`
  - reconciliation reason

Do not overwrite the canonical row’s source with “referral.” The result should say, in effect: one application, observed through both waitlist and referral provenance.

4. Reconcile the entitlement state

Do this in one transaction, with a lock or uniqueness constraint on the application’s current entitlement record.

First compare the two entitlement objects:

- entitlement values
- effective timestamps
- source event IDs
- object creation timestamps
- any status history
- whether either object was already marked current

Then apply this rule:

- The canonical entitlement object remains the one current entitlement state.
- The duplicate entitlement object is marked `superseded_duplicate` or equivalent and linked to the canonical object.
- Preserve its original payload and audit history; do not hard-delete it.
- If the values differ, resolve the value from the authoritative intake or entitlement event, not from `plan_name`, row order, or the later referral alone.
- If there is no authoritative resolution for a conflict, stop release for this pair and send it to the documented ops-review path rather than silently inventing a state.

The final invariant must be:

- exactly one current entitlement state for the canonical application
- zero current entitlement states for the duplicate alias
- both original entitlement objects still traceable in history

This follows the existing rule that entitlement must be explicit and canonical; it must not be inferred from a display or plan name.

5. Reconcile the support state separately

Do the same comparison for support state, but do not merge support state into entitlement.

Because neither row has been routed to Customer Success, there should be no route or handoff event to preserve as a customer-facing action. Still verify that explicitly.

For the support objects:

- Keep one support-state object current under the canonical application.
- Mark the duplicate support-state object as superseded, retaining its original source and timestamps.
- Preserve any raw support events from both rows in history.
- If both support states are identical and have equivalent evidence, retain the canonical row’s object as current.
- If they differ, use the documented support-event precedence and effective timestamps to determine the current value. Do not choose based simply on the fact that the referral arrived 17 minutes later.
- Do not derive support state from activation, integration status, entitlement, or the presence of a referral.

The final invariant must be:

- exactly one current support state
- support state remains a separate object from entitlement
- no Customer Success route is created by the reconciliation

6. Cleanup sequence

A contained write sequence would be:

1. Begin a transaction.
2. Lock the two intake rows and their current entitlement/support records.
3. Recheck the duplicate predicate and event history.
4. Create or confirm the duplicate-group record.
5. Set the waitlist row as canonical.
6. Link the referral row as a duplicate alias.
7. Attach both provenance signals to the canonical application.
8. Retain exactly one current entitlement object.
9. Mark the duplicate entitlement object superseded.
10. Retain exactly one current support-state object.
11. Mark the duplicate support object superseded.
12. Add a reconciliation audit event containing before/after IDs and counts.
13. Commit.
14. Rerun the same reconciliation in dry-run mode to confirm it is idempotent.

Do not:

- delete the referral provenance
- create a third merged application
- copy the referral source over the waitlist source
- create an invitation
- create a Customer Success route
- alter any of the other 23 applications
- use `DISTINCT` alone as a substitute for application-level deduplication

7. Audit checks

Before release, verify all of the following.

Count and cap

- Raw intake rows remain 25.
- Unique applications are exactly 24.
- Exactly one duplicate group contains two rows.
- The company contributes one, and only one, application to the 120-cap denominator.
- The cap counter changes by one application, not two.
- No unrelated application changed count or status.

Provenance

- The canonical record points to the original waitlist row.
- The canonical record also points to the referral row.
- Both source channels, original timestamps, row IDs, and raw payload references remain available.
- The duplicate reason records the same-domain and same-admin-email match plus the 17-minute interval.
- No provenance field was silently replaced or discarded.

Entitlement

- One and only one entitlement is marked current.
- The duplicate entitlement is linked as superseded.
- The current value is explicit and source-backed.
- No entitlement was inferred from `plan_name`.
- The entitlement history contains both pre-reconciliation object IDs.

Support

- One and only one support state is current.
- The duplicate support object is superseded, not lost.
- No support state was derived from entitlement or activation.
- No Customer Success route or handoff event exists for either row.
- No new route was created during reconciliation.

Side effects and isolation

- Zero invitations were sent or queued for either row.
- Zero workspace records were created by either row.
- The other 23 applications are unchanged in row contents, child-object counts, statuses, and event history.
- No orphaned entitlement or support object remains attached to the duplicate alias as current.
- No current object points to both applications.

Rerun safety

- A second reconciliation run produces no additional writes.
- The pair still resolves to one canonical application.
- The cap denominator remains 24.
- No new entitlement, support, invitation, or routing objects are generated.

8. Release criteria

Release the pair back to normal intake processing only when:

- the 25-to-24 count reconciliation passes;
- the canonical waitlist record and both provenance signals are visible;
- exactly one current entitlement and one current support state remain;
- the duplicate child objects are preserved as superseded history;
- no invitation, workspace, or Customer Success route exists;
- all 23 unrelated applications pass an unchanged-record comparison;
- the cap calculation shows one application for this company;
- the operation passes an idempotent dry run; and
- an owner has reviewed any entitlement or support-state conflict rather than allowing an implicit choice.

The resulting readout should state: “25 raw intake rows reconciled to 24 unique applications; one waitlist/referral duplicate retained as a single canonical application with both provenance signals; one current entitlement state and one current support state restored; 23 other applications unchanged; no invitations or Customer Success routes created.”

input.body:
HISTORICAL CONTROLLED-INTAKE WORKSHEET
Helio Start | Archive date: 2028-01-01

SCOPE — READ FIRST
This worksheet records the historical, beta-only controlled-intake adjudication used for the January readiness cohort. It is a reviewer-training artifact for identity evidence, routing, and state integrity in that controlled archive. It is not universal guidance for every later Helio Start flow, public signup, GA process, pricing-page exposure, or future eligibility implementation. Do not retroactively recode earlier cohorts or apply this matrix without checking the governing rules for the later flow.

Historical reference: 30 held applications were classified as 18 exact-domain automatic passes, 9 legitimate parent-company or IT-managed cases that passed only after corroborating admin evidence, and 3 agency identities routed to Customer Success. The cohorts and denominators must remain separate.

DECISION MATRIX

| Sample row | Observed identity/domain evidence | Required adjudication | Routing/result | State-handling note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Exact-domain proof | OAuth identity domain exactly matches the established workspace/customer domain; applicant confirms admin ownership; no contradictory ownership, SSO, or delegation signal. | Treat as strong automatic proof for this historical controlled intake. Record the exact source evidence and identity. | Admit to the controlled reviewed path; continue normal pre-setup checks. | A domain match proves only the historical identity-evidence condition; it does not by itself establish entitlement, support state, or later-flow eligibility. |
| Legitimate parent-company or IT-managed domain mismatch | OAuth domain differs from workspace/customer domain because ownership sits with a parent company, business unit, or IT-managed SSO arrangement; corroborating admin evidence identifies who controls the relevant workspace/integration administration. | Do not auto-fail and do not auto-pass. Validate the relationship and retain the corroborating evidence. | If corroborated, admit to the controlled reviewed path. If control remains unresolved, route to Customer Success before setup. | Preserve both domains, SSO/admin context, evidence source, and adjudication reason; do not collapse this into an exact-domain pass. |
| Agency identity | Applicant authenticates with an agency/third-party domain or is acting for a client; written authorization may show permission to assist but does not make the agency employee the client’s eligible workspace admin. | Do not accept self-attestation as customer-admin proof. Distinguish agency/client administration from an ordinary domain mismatch. | Route to Customer Success/assisted setup before workspace setup; involve the client’s authorized administrator. | Do not admit through the self-serve controlled path merely because the integration is supported or authorization is attached. |
| Missing current-state data | Entitlement or support state is blank, stale, ambiguous, conflicting, or not source-backed at adjudication time. A blank support state is not evidence of no support need. | Fail closed for the affected decision. Preserve raw events and timestamps; do not infer from plan name, activation, invitation status, or the other state. | Hold the row until reconciled, or route to the documented ops/Customer Success review path. Eligibility remains pending until both states are current. | Keep entitlement and support state separate. Record an operational exception; never manufacture a state to complete the row. |

ADJUDICATION RULES FOR REVIEWERS
1. Exact-domain match is positive evidence, not a universal ownership determination.
2. A legitimate mismatch requires corroborating evidence of control; ambiguity is not a pass.
3. Agency, contractor, delegated, or third-party identities cannot qualify through self-attestation alone.
4. Preserve original identifiers and provenance. Annotate ambiguous historical rows rather than silently recoding them.
5. A missing or conflicting state fails closed. Do not treat null as “none.”
6. Keep identity adjudication, entitlement, and support state as separate decisions.

FINAL ENTITLEMENT AND SUPPORT-STATE VALIDATION CHECKS
Before a row is admitted, invited, or included in a historical readout, verify:

[ ] Identity and population
    - One distinct application/workspace identity is represented; no duplicate, cross-workspace join, or merged record.
    - The evidence tier and routing result are explicitly recorded.
    - Original domain, email, SSO/admin context, evidence IDs, and adjudication reason are retained.

[ ] Entitlement
    - Exactly one current entitlement state exists for the application/workspace.
    - The state is explicit and source-backed; it is not inferred from plan_name, an invitation, activation, or cash/billing display.
    - Conflicting or missing entitlement data remains unknown/pending and blocks the decision.

[ ] Support state
    - Exactly one current support state exists, separately from entitlement.
    - The state is current, source-backed, and linked to the correct application/workspace.
    - A blank, stale, or ambiguous support state is unresolved—not “no active support need”—and blocks eligibility/invitation until reconciled.
    - Raw support events, route/handoff events, timestamps, and queue diagnostics remain available for audit.

[ ] Release and audit
    - No invitation or state-changing action occurs while either required current state is unresolved.
    - Current-state derivation uses the valid authoritative event/state and does not count superseded provisional or duplicate states as additional current rows.
    - Each row contributes to one mutually exclusive current routing outcome; exception details remain in the audit view, not as a fabricated current state.
    - Reconciliation leaves no blank, duplicate, merged, or orphaned current state.

HISTORICAL BOUNDARY
Use this worksheet to understand and audit the controlled-intake archive only. For any later Helio Start Start flow, re-check its contemporaneous product, policy, evidence, entitlement, support, and routing rules; do not assume this matrix is still the operative decision logic.

sources.label: Assistant's reply to Riley Tanaka, message 001653
excerpts:
G should be treated as ineligible/suppressed for the dry run, despite having all three signals. Its qualifying event was performed by an admin who is no longer active, so historical activity alone cannot satisfy the current active-admin requirement.

Owen should add a current-status join/filter before the final rerun:

```sql
JOIN workspace_memberships m
  ON m.workspace_id = activity.workspace_id
 AND m.user_id = activity.actor_user_id
WHERE activity.actor_type = 'human'
  AND activity.is_admin_action = TRUE
  AND activity.occurred_at >= evaluation_time - INTERVAL '30 days'
  AND m.status = 'active'
  AND m.role IN ('admin', 'owner')
  AND (m.deactivated_at IS NULL OR m.deactivated_at > evaluation_time)
```

The check must be evaluated at the eligibility timestamp, not merely at the time of the historical event. Missing, unmapped, deactivated, suspended, or non-admin current status should fail closed for the active-admin signal. G can remain in the audit output with its event and deactivation details, but it must not be marked eligible.

input.title: Expansion Assist July pilot — eligibility audit worksheet
input.body:
Historical eligibility audit worksheet

Pilot scope and source of truth
- Pilot: approved Expansion Assist July 8 bounded pilot.
- Historical source of truth: approved pilot decision and the final validated eligibility implementation recorded in the Expansion Assist pilot measurement brief (BRIEF-2024-04-expansion-assist-pilot-measurement).
- Eligibility review only: this worksheet covers selection controls and eligibility fixtures. It does not make exposure, handoff, expansion, causal, pipeline, revenue, or forecast claims.
- Approved boundary: at most 30 retained mid-segment accounts; an account must satisfy all three readiness signals and have no active Customer Success suppression. Behavior readiness replaces account-age/day-60 eligibility.

Required current-state controls
1. Three-signal requirement
   - Deeper integration use is present.
   - A product-visible usage-ceiling crossing is present.
   - Recent qualifying human-admin activity is present.
   - All three signals are required; a missing signal fails closed.

2. Recent active human-admin control
   - Evaluate qualifying activity within the approved recent window: the prior 30 days relative to the eligibility timestamp.
   - Activity must be a human admin action; service-token-only activity does not qualify.
   - Join the activity actor to current workspace membership at the eligibility timestamp.
   - The actor must map to an active human member with admin or owner role.
   - The member must not be deactivated at evaluation; suspended, missing, unmapped, stale, conflicting, or otherwise invalid current status fails closed.
   - Do not satisfy the control from historical activity alone when the actor is no longer active. Evaluate current status at the eligibility timestamp, not only at the historical event time.

3. Current Customer Success suppression
   - Suppress when current Customer Success adoption work or renewal work is active.
   - Read the current state, not only a stale nightly suppression table.
   - Stale, missing, or conflicting adoption/renewal records fail closed rather than clearing suppression.

4. Selection and audit treatment
   - Retain the original locked primary cohort and report eligibility separately from any other pilot measure.
   - Preserve the final validated rerun treatment: 28 eligible locked-primary accounts; reserve 1 remains suppressed for active renewal work; reserves 2 and 3 remain available for the two operational slots.
   - Keep ineligible or suppressed fixture records in the audit output with the failing control and reason; do not mark them eligible.

Validated fixture cases

Case A — PASS
- Fixture: human admin active 3 days ago; all three readiness signals present; no active Customer Success work.
- Expected decision: Pass / eligible.
- Reason: qualifying recent human-admin activity, all three required signals, and no current CS suppression.

Case B — FAIL
- Fixture: service token active 1 day ago; last human-admin activity 62 days ago; all other signals present; no active Customer Success work.
- Expected decision: Fail / ineligible.
- Reason: activity is service-token-only for the recent period; the last human-admin activity is outside the 30-day window.

Case C — FAIL
- Fixture: human admin active 45 days ago; all other signals present; no active Customer Success work.
- Expected decision: Fail / ineligible.
- Reason: qualifying human-admin activity is stale and outside the 30-day window.

Case D — FAIL
- Fixture: human admin active 2 days ago; all three readiness signals present; renewal work opened yesterday afternoon; nightly suppression table still says none.
- Expected decision: Fail / suppressed.
- Reason: current Customer Success renewal work is active; current state overrides the stale nightly suppression value.

Case E — FAIL
- Fixture: human admin active 5 days ago; integration-depth and active-admin signals present; no product-visible usage-ceiling signal.
- Expected decision: Fail / ineligible.
- Reason: the three-signal requirement is not met because the usage-ceiling signal is missing.

Case F — PASS
- Fixture: human admin active 1 day ago; all three readiness signals present; no active Customer Success work.
- Expected decision: Pass / eligible.
- Reason: qualifying recent human-admin activity, all three required signals, and no current CS suppression.

Case G — FAIL
- Fixture: historical qualifying activity was generated by a human admin who is no longer active; all three readiness signals present.
- Expected decision: Fail / ineligible.
- Reason: the current-user-status join shows the qualifying admin is deactivated. Historical activity alone cannot satisfy the current active-human-admin control.

Validation result
- Independently validated fixture suite: A and F pass; B, C, D, E, and G fail for the reasons above.
- Fail-closed rule: stale or conflicting adoption and renewal records, and missing, unmapped, deactivated, suspended, or non-admin current user status, must not inherit or preserve eligibility.

sources.label: Assistant's reply to Riley Tanaka, message 001464
excerpts:
Tomás — we should not treat “Not sure” as “Yes” or admit those applicants while asking Setup Support to resolve access afterward.

The connector-access check is part of first-week integration fit. Admission should mean the applicant can definitely authenticate the selected connector during setup—not merely that access might become available later. “No” and “Not sure” therefore remain pending before admission and are routed to assistance. They are not rejected, and no credentials or secrets are collected.

The early operating read does not show avoidable friction that justifies changing that boundary. Among the first 31 starts after the check, 24 answered “Yes,” four answered “No,” and three answered “Not sure.” All seven uncertain cases were held before admission. Three later obtained access and changed to “Yes”; two still required assisted handling; and two remained pending. No workspace was admitted while its answer was “No” or “Not sure.” That shows the route is functioning as designed: uncertain access is being identified, separated from the admitted cohort, and worked through assistance. It does not show that holding those cases was harmful or that they would have been successful if admitted.

The earlier GA audit is another reason not to relax the rule. Of 147 admitted workspaces, 31 failed to complete a supported first integration by day seven, and 18 of those had Helio-admin proof but lacked the third-party credentials for their selected connector. That is evidence that workspace administration and connector access are different readiness conditions—not evidence that connector uncertainty should be admitted.

Changing the rule now would also mix two separate decisions: the admission policy and an untested goal of increasing immediate volume. A higher admitted count could simply mean that unresolved access risk has been moved downstream, where it would appear as failed activation, delayed setup, or additional support work. It would not establish better conversion, revenue, retention, or pipeline quality.

The defensible approach is to keep “Not sure” pending, measure assisted resolution and subsequent admission separately, and evaluate day-seven supported integration once there is enough operating evidence. The early counts confirm that the routing mechanism works; they do not justify weakening pre-admission handling.

results.content:
Helio Start Q3 closeout — meeting frame

Opening frame

“We are closing Q3 on what the current operating model can support, what it cannot support, and whether we agree to keep Q4 as a controlled learning beta. This is not a launch or pricing decision, and the admin path is not solved.”

1. What Helio Start has support for

- A narrow, non-public controlled beta for selected sub-50-seat accounts.
- Entry through the invite path, not the public pricing page.
- Candidates with complete eligibility information, simple deployment, and a clear named administrator.
- Earlier admin-ownership proof as a customer-protective gate. It prevents avoidable support handoffs; it does not mean the underlying admin experience is solved.
- Ordinary integration and API-key/setup questions handled through docs-first support.
- Explicit routing for entitlement, support, billing, and lifecycle state.
- Separate measurement of sub-50 activation, support load, and retained-mid performance.
- Conservative lifecycle communication that does not create a state-changing or support promise beyond the beta boundary.

2. What Helio Start does not support

- It does not support a general self-serve path when admin ownership or permissions are unclear.
- It does not support manual billing exceptions.
- It does not support migration or import assistance inside the beta path.
- It does not support treating seat count alone as eligibility.
- It does not support assuming the admin path is fixed because proof is now collected earlier.
- It does not support public pricing-page exposure, paid acquisition, or broad beta widening.
- It does not support launch language, a Q4 revenue claim, forecast credit, or retrospective Q3 revenue credit.
- It does not support folding Helio Start into the retained-mid or Expansion Assist read.
- Unresolved cases should be held out of the self-serve beta and routed to the appropriate assisted path—not forced through as edge cases.

3. Q4 controlled-beta operating shape to ask Tomás to accept

Ask Tomás to accept this:

“Keep Helio Start capped and non-public through Q4 as a controlled operating-model beta. Admit only accounts that meet the documented deployment, eligibility, and admin-proof requirements. Treat unclear admin ownership, permissions complexity, billing exceptions, and migration/import needs as assisted paths. Review activation together with support-load mix and handoff quality, with no pricing-page exposure, paid acquisition, launch framing, or revenue/forecast credit. Revisit widening only after the admin-ownership and support evidence is durable enough to show that we are reducing avoidable handoffs—not merely moving the check earlier.”

Decision to leave the room with

- Tomás accepts “capped controlled beta” as the Q4 posture.
- The admin-proof check is accepted as a guardrail, not represented as a solved admin experience.
- Daniela, Owen, Ines, and Support retain explicit operating owners for entitlement/state, measurement, lifecycle, and handoffs.
- Any future widening requires a separate evidence-based gate; it is not implied by Q4 planning.

input.body:
Historical baseline
Effective: 2024-04-23
Path: Helio Start intake reached from the public pricing page
Status: regression-lineage card; historical baseline, not a later policy change

Admission predicates (each is an independent input)
I1  Account is under 50 seats.
I2  Helio admin access/ownership is verified with acceptable admin proof.
I3  Deployment is simple/supported.
I4  A supported first integration can be connected within the first week.
I5  Entitlement state is current.
I6  Billing is supported/standard; no manual-billing exception.
I7  Ownership is clear and standard permissions are sufficient; no unresolved ownership.
I8  Applicant is for its own organization; not an agency/consultant or cross-organization administrator.
I9  No import is needed.
I10 No migration is needed.
I11 No unsupported, advanced, shared, or nonstandard permissions are needed.
I12 Later connector-access input: applicant or an available owner can definitely authenticate the selected connector (answer = Yes). Connector No or Not sure remains pending and routes to assistance before workspace admission; it is not admitted.

Regression cases
A0 — ADMITTED — all inputs present
I1–I12 are present. Expected result: continues through the otherwise unchanged eligibility checks and may be admitted after review. No credentials or secrets are collected.

N1 — NOT ADMITTED — I1 missing
All of I2–I12 present; account is 50+ seats. Expected: route out of the Helio Start self-serve path.
N2 — NOT ADMITTED — I2 missing
All of I1 and I3–I12 present; admin proof is absent or unacceptable. Expected: pending/assisted review; no admission.
N3 — NOT ADMITTED — I3 missing
All other inputs present; deployment is complex or unsupported. Expected: route out/assisted path.
N4 — NOT ADMITTED — I4 missing
All other inputs present; no supported first-week integration fit. Expected: route out/assisted path.
N5 — NOT ADMITTED — I5 missing
All other inputs present; entitlement state is missing, stale, or not current. Expected: hold pending; no admission.
N6 — NOT ADMITTED — I6 missing
All other inputs present; manual billing or another unsupported billing condition is required. Expected: route to assistance before setup; no admission.
N7 — NOT ADMITTED — I7 missing
All other inputs present; ownership is unresolved or standard permissions are insufficient. Expected: pending/ownership-permissions review; no admission.
N8 — NOT ADMITTED — I8 missing
All other inputs present; applicant is an agency/consultant or cross-organization administrator. Expected: ineligible for Start self-serve / route out.
N9 — NOT ADMITTED — I9 missing
All other inputs present; import is required. Expected: route to assisted path before setup; no admission.
N10 — NOT ADMITTED — I10 missing
All other inputs present; migration is required. Expected: route to assisted path before setup; no admission.
N11 — NOT ADMITTED — I11 missing
All other inputs present; unsupported, advanced, shared, or nonstandard permissions are required. Expected: route out/assisted path; no admission.
N12 — NOT ADMITTED — I12 missing
All other inputs present; connector-access answer is No or Not sure rather than a definite Yes. Expected: remain pending and route to Customer Success assistance before workspace admission; no admission.

Lineage rules
- Each N case removes exactly one input and keeps every other input present; no two missing inputs are combined.
- A definite connector-access Yes continues through the otherwise unchanged checks. Connector authentication is stored separately from Helio admin proof.
- This card preserves the 2024-04-23 public-path boundary: agency identities, unresolved ownership, manual billing, imports, migrations, unsupported permissions, and other existing route-out conditions remain unchanged.
- Completing the intake does not itself guarantee admission or workspace access.

sources.label: Assistant's reply to Riley Tanaka, message 001787
excerpts:
Marcus — I would not approve the $100,000 Q3 paid-acquisition test or attach a pipeline claim to this result.

The completed Helio Start cohort supports a bounded organic conclusion:

- 52 of 52 workspaces have mature day-90 windows.
- 39 were paid and active at the day-90 snapshot.
- 7 had canceled before day 90.
- 4 were past due.
- 2 were on billing hold.

The four statuses reconcile to the full cohort. The 39/52 result is therefore useful descriptive evidence that Helio Start can operate as an organic pricing-page product motion. It is not, by itself, a retention-rate, acquisition, causal, or pipeline result.

The acquisition and pipeline leap is not decision-safe for three reasons:

1. No acquisition-cost comparison exists. This is an organic cohort, so we do not know what paid spend would be required to produce comparable workspaces, what the incremental conversion would be, or whether the motion could support acceptable CAC, payback, contribution margin, or LTV/CAC.

2. First-paid, activation, and paid-active answer different questions from unit economics. First-paid establishes that a qualifying payment occurred; activation establishes product behavior; paid-active establishes billing/entitlement status at a specified snapshot. None establishes revenue durability, gross margin, support or servicing cost, acquisition cost, payback period, or forecastable lifetime value.

3. The denominator cannot be narrowed to the favorable status. Omitting the 7 canceled, 4 past-due, and 2 billing-hold workspaces would turn a complete 52-workspace status table into an unsupported success claim and would obscure material outcome states.

Decision: keep Helio Start available as a bounded organic pricing-page channel through Q3, with the existing refusal rules and connector-access check. Do not authorize the $100,000 paid-acquisition test or create a Q3 pipeline claim from this cohort. Reconsider only after we have a defined paid test or credible acquisition-cost benchmark, incremental attribution, revenue and margin data, and mature retention/payback evidence.

results.content:
Finance’s package supports only a narrow set of test-budget calculations:

- Media spend: $24,000
- One-time creative/setup cost: $2,400
- Total proposed test cost: $26,400
- Qualified signup-start target: 160
- Media cost per qualified signup start: $150
- Setup cost allocated per qualified signup start: $15
- Fully loaded cost per qualified signup start: $165

The $165 figure assumes the entire one-time setup cost is allocated to this 160-start test. These are planning inputs, not observed acquisition results.

What cannot be calculated:

- Paid activation rate or paid-activation count: Finance supplied no expected or observed activation count.
- Cost per activation, paid CAC, or cost per retained account: there is no activation, paid-customer, or mature-account denominator.
- Refund-adjusted cash or net cash: the package has no revenue assumption and no treatment for later refunds.
- Revenue, margin, contribution, payback, or LTV/CAC: the required cash, margin, retention, and lifetime inputs are absent.
- Support effort or servicing cost: there is no support-volume, handling-time, or account-level support assumption.
- Account-level paid-channel quality: there are no account IDs, attribution fields, retention outcomes, or support joins tying paid starts to later outcomes.

Gate assessment: not satisfied.

The standing paid-acquisition gate requires mature retention status together with refund-adjusted cash and account-level support effort. The September 9 package contains none of those outcome lanes; it contains only proposed spend, setup cost, and a signup-start target. It therefore cannot establish the evidence required to accept paid acquisition.

The existing Helio Start evidence does provide mature organic-cohort status, matched refund-adjusted cash, and classified account-level support effort. However, that evidence remains organic and cannot be relabeled as paid-channel performance. The Finance package does not supply the missing paid-channel bridge—paid activation and retention outcomes, refund-adjusted paid cash, and account-level paid support effort or a credible paid comparison.

Decision-safe conclusion: use the package to describe a proposed $26,400 test and a fully loaded $165 cost per qualified signup start, but do not treat it as paid CAC, a paid-acquisition evidence submission, or authorization to launch the test.

input.title: Helio Start 2028 paid-acquisition proposal readiness checklist
input.body:
Purpose

Reusable gate for every 2028 Helio Start paid-acquisition proposal. Do not discuss a budget amount, paid channel, audience, targeting, bid, or other channel tactic until every required evidence condition below is marked PASS. A PASS permits a proposal discussion only; it does not approve budget, paid traffic, launch, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, or a paid-acquisition claim.

Readiness checklist

[ ] 1. Mature retention/status evidence is complete
- The admitted cohort has complete mature windows, normally day 90.
- The exact admission and observation dates are recorded.
- Every admitted workspace is included in the denominator and assigned one mutually exclusive status; do not report only paid-active or another favorable subset.
- The status table reconciles to the full admitted cohort.
- If the standing reopening gate applies, use two consecutive mature qualifying cohorts, not one isolated packet.

[ ] 2. Refund-adjusted cash evidence is complete
- Gross billed cash, refunds, and refund-adjusted collected cash are shown separately.
- Refunds are mapped to the relevant workspace/account; unmatched aggregate refunds do not pass the gate.
- The cash observation window and treatment are documented.

[ ] 3. Account-level support-effort evidence is complete
- Post-admission support effort is measured for every admitted workspace, including zero-contact workspaces.
- Account-level minutes, distribution, and high-effort cases are shown; do not report only contacted accounts.
- Pre-admission connector/authority assistance, billing contacts, and other excluded work are kept distinct from post-admission product-support effort.
- High-support cases are classified and any unsupported admitted case is explicitly identified. For the standing two-cohort reopening condition, each qualifying cohort must have fewer than 5% of accounts above 90 support minutes and no unsupported admitted case.

[ ] 4. Paid-acquisition bridge evidence is complete
- There is observed paid acquisition cost or a credible acquisition-cost benchmark.
- Paid-source attribution is credible and incremental: paid starts, assisted routes, admissions, attribution failures, and later outcomes are separately counted and reconciled.
- Incremental outcome evidence is available; organic-cohort outcomes cannot be relabeled as paid performance.
- Where the proposal makes unit-economic or payback claims, revenue, margin/contribution, and mature payback evidence are present and the assumptions are explicit.

[ ] 5. Source and limitation checks pass
- Each number traces to a dated source record and a defined cohort/account denominator.
- Retention/status, refund-adjusted cash, support effort, and paid-source evidence remain separately visible; do not collapse them into a blended score.
- First-paid, activation, day-7 first integration, or paid-active status alone is not sufficient.
- Missing maturity, unmapped refunds, unsupported admissions, weak attribution, or immature leading indicators means NOT READY.

How the evidence must be combined

Use one decision package containing all required evidence for the same defined cohort or explicitly matched cohorts. Join cash and support measures at account/workspace level; reconcile every denominator and total; preserve the mutually exclusive status table; and show the paid-acquisition bridge alongside, not in place of, the mature operating evidence. Keep each measure analytically distinct so that cash is not treated as retention, support effort is not treated as acquisition cost, and organic results are not treated as paid-channel results.

The package must state what the evidence does and does not establish. It may support consideration of a bounded paid-acquisition proposal only after the full gate passes. It may not, by itself, create a budget approval, launch authorization, pipeline target, forecast credit, or scale conclusion.

Approved responsibility

Owen and Customer Success jointly own producing and maintaining the combined evidence package. This is one joint package responsibility, not separate owners for retention, cash, support, attribution, or any other evidence category. They must deliver the measures together, keep the account-level joins and distinctions intact, and mark the package READY or NOT READY against this checklist.

A proposal may be assembled or submitted only through the separately approved decision path. No person or team is assigned an additional category-specific ownership role by this checklist.

input.body:
CS auto-nudge historical replay — evidence scorecard
As of: January 1, 2028
Replay reference: April 24, 2025 historical replay against the shared-state contract

Purpose
Reconcile legacy-result matches, field-specific holds, and suppressions using a one-decision/one-count denominator. This is system-control evidence only; it is not customer-impact, conversion, revenue, causal, or mature-reliability evidence.

Scorecard

Top-level outcome                         Count
Legacy-result matches                       386
Non-matches / contract differences           26
Grand total                                 412

Non-match decomposition

Non-match parent                         Count
Field-specific holds                         19
Suppressions                                  7
Non-matches / contract differences           26

Field-specific holds: cause subtotals

Cause under field-specific holds          Count
Stale qualifying-human-admin state           15
Unresolved external-system authority           4
Field-specific holds subtotal                 19

Suppressions: cause subtotals

Cause under suppressions                  Count
Active Customer Success adoption or
renewal work                                  7
Suppressions subtotal                          7

Reconciliation checks

1. Hold causes to hold category:
   15 + 4 = 19. PASS.

2. Suppression causes to suppression category:
   7 = 7. PASS.

3. Non-match parents to non-match total:
   19 + 7 = 26. PASS.

4. Top-level outcomes to grand total:
   386 + 26 = 412. PASS.

5. Fully expanded grand total:
   386 + 15 + 4 + 7 = 412. PASS.

Interpretation of non-matches under the shared-state contract

The 26 non-matches are not unexplained mismatches or unclassified records. They are the contract's operating consequences where the legacy eligibility result would have allowed the decision to proceed but the shared-state rules prevented that outcome:

- 19 became visible, field-specific holds because required state was not safe to consume: 15 had stale qualifying-human-admin state and 4 had unresolved external-system authority. The contract fails closed and exposes the responsible field/reason rather than allowing an unsupported decision.
- 7 became suppressions because current Customer Success adoption or renewal work was active. Suppression is a valid current-state outcome, not a data-quality failure.

In other words, non-match means the legacy result differed from the governed, current-state disposition. It does not mean the replay failed to match records, lost data, or found a disputed field meaning.

Current-and-supported-state outcome check

No record with all required state current and supported changed outcome. The changed outcomes were confined to the stale or unresolved required-state holds and the active-Customer-Success-work suppressions. The replay therefore supports the conclusion that the contract prevented unsupported or conflicting decisions from proceeding; it does not support a claim that valid current-state decisions were altered.

Evidence boundary

The replay shows operating control: a complete denominator, explicit fail-closed holds, and valid suppressions. It should not be presented as proof of customer impact, conversion lift, revenue effect, causality, or mature reliability.

input.body:
Historical example — 2023-04-03

Audience
Priya, in a 1:1.

What was confirmed
EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger cleared the second cohort. The second-cohort cut was +3.4 pts in week-1 retention for treatment vs. control (n=200); pooled across both cohorts, the lift was +3.1 pts, p=0.04, n=420. I called the result positive and we began drafting the ship plan, with 100% rollout planned for Apr 10 if the remaining checks were clean.

My interpretation
Cautiously optimistic: the result had moved past the “maybe noise” phase and looked real/material enough to matter, but this was not premature certainty. I wanted the data to earn the next level of confidence, so I was still treating the first post-ship cohort as a watch-only stabilization read—not as a foregone win.

Evidence still wanted
Before fully trusting the result, I wanted one more clean, fully matured post-ship cohort (a full week) and the remaining integrity/guardrail checks: sample-ratio mismatch, signup-source mix, country/device or other segment skew, activation completion, and support touches. The onboarding-trigger read remained scope-disjoint from pricing_page_2023q2_rev; no attribution was being merged across them. The boundary was: confirmed positive and credible enough to plan the ship, not yet proof of durable rollout impact.

# Helio Start leadership readout — Jun 22

## Current call
Helio Start is a working name for the sub-50-seat motion. It is still pre-discovery, not a pricing-page launch, beta, or cheap-plan promise.

## Gate newly added from engineering scoping
Before any pricing-page experiment or launch, we need clean event taxonomy and entitlement instrumentation for admin complexity, import or migration help, support handoff, and entitlement state. Any later pricing-page test also needs to obey the no-concurrent-layout/UI-change rule.

Use activation definition v3. Keep 75-200-seat mid-seg v2 separate. Show the 50-75-seat band separately. 1. Accept instrumentation as a hard gate before pricing-page experiment or launch.
2. Keep billing exceptions and manual import/migration needs in the refusal-risk model for June.
3. Keep lifecycle work at fork mapping until eligibility and state-changing paths are clearer.

## Not decisions this week
No public pricing-page copy. No Q3 launch commitment. No change to retained-mid expansion-nudge eligibility.

## Open questions
Engineering: event taxonomy, entitlement state, dashboarding, and sizing.
Lifecycle: where the onboarding path must fork without creating support promises.

results.content:
Migration risk: HIGH but manageable with a staged rollout.

The failure mode is silent rather than obvious: beginning April 15, `workspace.plan_name` will stop updating. A template can continue rendering successfully while showing an old or incorrect plan name. Risk is elevated by:

- Three affected production paths: renewal reminder, integration summary, and trial-expiry education.
- Two unresolved accountable-owner gaps: integration summary and trial-expiry education.
- Same-name template collisions with distinct production IDs and histories.
- Existing renewal-reminder sensitivity, including the prior localized rendering hold.
- A hard dependency on the April 15 behavior change.

Do not treat the display name as an identifier. Work from the production template ID, workflow reference, audience, and lifecycle state. Do not merge, rename, retire, or edit same-name records as part of this migration.

Sequenced plan

1. Establish the inventory and release boundary

Owner: Ines
Implementation/release controls: Daniela
Documentation contractor: preparation only; no production changes or approval authority

Before any template is edited:

- Export each affected template by production ID.
- Record its workflow, audience, trigger, suppression rules, current state, and last-send evidence.
- Search the full workspace for both `workspace.plan_name` and `entitlement.display_name`.
- Identify every reference, including shared snippets and conditional branches.
- Map each record to a display-only handoff label:
  - Renewal reminder — current production path
  - Integration summary — Active
  - Trial expiry — Customer Success or Self-serve, based on the documented route
- Keep the retired `Integration summary` record separate from the active record.
- Keep the Customer Success and self-serve `Trial expiry` records separate.
- Mark the two unresolved records:
  - `OWNER NOT DOCUMENTED — ACCOUNTABILITY UNCONFIRMED`
  - `RELEASE AUTHORITY NOT ESTABLISHED`

Exit gate: a production-ID-level inventory exists, and every affected reference is accounted for. No production edit before this gate.

2. Resolve ownership and business acceptance

Renewal reminder:
- Business owner: Customer Success operations, as documented in the current runbook.
- Technical implementation and release controls: Daniela.
- Preview, rendered-copy review, and routine preflight: Ines.
- Customer Success must confirm the intended plan-label behavior and fallback copy.

Integration summary:
- No accountable owner is currently evidenced.
- An old folder creator is not an owner.
- Route the active production record for an authorized ownership and release decision before implementation.
- Do not infer ownership from the active status or from the display name.
- Confirm that the retired 2024 record is not referenced before touching the active record.

Trial-expiry education:
- No approved owner is currently evidenced.
- A recent editor is not an accountable owner.
- First confirm whether the affected record is the self-serve education path or the Customer Success-routed path.
- Because “education” alone does not establish non-state-changing behavior, confirm the trigger, state-writing behavior, audience, and dependencies.
- Keep the record on hold if any of those remain unclear.

Exit gate: each production record has a named accountable business owner and an authorized release decision. Until then, the two unresolved records remain review-only.

3. Implement and preview the renewal reminder first

Owner: Daniela
Business acceptance: Customer Success operations
Preview/preflight: Ines

Use an isolated draft or preview version. Replace only the plan-name reference with `entitlement.display_name`; do not make unrelated copy or logic changes.

Required preview matrix:

- Entitlement has the expected populated display name.
- `workspace.plan_name` and `entitlement.display_name` intentionally disagree; the entitlement value must win.
- Entitlement is null or missing while the old workspace value is populated; confirm the approved fallback and ensure the stale workspace value is not silently used.
- Entitlement display name is empty or whitespace-only.
- The recipient is suppressed or otherwise outside the send audience.
- Existing renewal-specific links, dates, audience conditions, and suppression behavior remain unchanged.
- Rendered copy does not reintroduce the prior malformed greeting or other whitespace issue.

Release gate:

- All expected renders pass.
- Customer Success accepts the populated, missing, and mismatch cases.
- Ines records the preflight and suppression evidence.
- Daniela records the exact production change and release version.
- Keep only this affected send path held if the gate fails; do not pause unrelated lifecycle programs.

4. Implement and preview the active integration summary second

Owner: authorized owner to be appointed
Technical implementation/release controls: Daniela
Preview/preflight: Ines

Before editing:

- Confirm the active production ID.
- Confirm that the retired 2024 template is not referenced by the active workflow or any scheduled path.
- Confirm whether the active template has any state-changing behavior or downstream dependency.
- Preserve the retired record and its history unchanged.

Required preview matrix:

- Active integration summary with a populated entitlement display name.
- Workspace and entitlement values deliberately mismatched.
- Missing or null entitlement with an approved fallback.
- Empty or whitespace-only display name.
- Multiple-integration and no-integration fixtures, if those branches exist.
- Suppressed recipient and excluded-audience fixtures.
- Confirmation that the retired production ID is neither edited nor selected by the workflow.
- Comparison against the pre-migration output for all unrelated copy and links.

Release gate:

- Authorized owner and release authority are documented.
- Active-versus-retired object selection is proven by ID.
- Preview and suppression evidence passes.
- No inferred ownership or “same name” shortcut is used.

5. Implement and preview trial-expiry education third

Owner: authorized owner to be appointed
Technical implementation/release controls: Daniela
Preview/preflight: Ines, with the route owner

First resolve the route and semantics:

- Confirm whether this is the self-serve education record or Customer Success-routed record.
- Confirm whether the template only informs or can change eligibility, trial state, routing, or another customer state.
- Confirm dependencies and suppression conditions.
- If any of these are unclear, classify it as `REQUIRES REVIEW` and do not release.

Required preview matrix:

- Correct route with a populated entitlement display name.
- A mismatched stale `workspace.plan_name` versus current entitlement value.
- Missing, null, and whitespace-only entitlement values.
- Users at the edge of the trial-expiry eligibility condition.
- Suppressed, converted, or otherwise excluded users.
- Self-serve and Customer Success paths tested independently where both exist.
- Verification that the change does not alter state-writing behavior, eligibility, routing, or suppression.
- Confirmation that the sibling same-name record was not edited.

Release gate:

- Ownership and release authority are established.
- State-writing and dependency review is complete.
- The correct production ID and audience are proven.
- All rendered-copy and behavioral previews pass.

6. Run a combined regression and production-preview pass

Owners: Ines and Daniela
Business sign-off: each authorized template owner

Run the three templates together only after their individual gates pass.

The final evidence pack should include:

- Production ID and unchanged canonical name.
- Old and new field references.
- Before/after rendered output.
- Populated, mismatch, null, missing, and whitespace cases.
- Audience and suppression results.
- Trigger and state-writing comparison.
- Active/retired or route-specific object verification.
- Owner and release-authority evidence.
- Exact release version and timestamp.
- Rollback or hold procedure.

The most important test is the deliberate mismatch case. If the preview still shows the old `workspace.plan_name` value, the migration has not succeeded even if the message renders without an error.

7. Release in separate waves

Recommended order:

1. Renewal reminder, because it has a documented business owner and the clearest operational path.
2. Active integration summary, only after its ownership gap and active-versus-retired reference check are resolved.
3. Trial-expiry education, only after its route, state-writing behavior, and release authority are confirmed.

Do not release all three in one production change. Keep each template independently reversible or independently holdable. A rollback to `workspace.plan_name` is not a reliable long-term fallback after April 15 because that field will no longer receive current updates; rollback should mean reverting the template version or holding the send path, not returning to a stale data source.

Final recommendation

Treat the renewal reminder as the first controlled migration wave. Treat integration summary and trial-expiry education as governance-blocked until authorized owners are named. The migration should be considered complete only when a full-workspace scan finds no remaining active references in these three paths, all three have production-ID-level evidence, and the mismatch previews prove that `entitlement.display_name`—not a stale workspace field—is driving the rendered value.

input.title: 2028 Lifecycle QA Specification — Entitlement-Name Regression
input.body:
Date: 2028-01-01
Status: QA specification
Scope: Renewal reminder; Trial-expiry education; Integration summary.

Objective
Verify that all three active lifecycle templates render the current entitlement name consistently across populated and missing-data states, without changing unrelated lifecycle behavior.

Rendering contract
- Authoritative source: entitlement.display_name. This is the only field permitted to drive the entitlement name.
- Populated value: render the supplied entitlement.display_name exactly.
- Missing, null, empty-string, or whitespace-only value: render the neutral fallback "your plan".
- Deliberate mismatch: when entitlement.display_name and any legacy value differ, entitlement.display_name must win.
- Legacy source prohibited: workspace.plan_name must never be referenced, used as a fallback, or control any rendered branch. A passing message that displays a stale workspace value is a failure.

Required regression matrix
Run independently against the exact active production template/version for each of the three templates:

1. entitlement.display_name = "Pro Annual"; workspace.plan_name absent
   Expected: "Pro Annual".
2. entitlement.display_name = "Pro Annual"; workspace.plan_name = "Legacy Basic"
   Expected: "Pro Annual"; proves the authoritative source wins.
3. entitlement.display_name missing; workspace.plan_name = "Legacy Basic"
   Expected: "your plan"; proves no legacy fallback.
4. entitlement.display_name = null; workspace.plan_name = "Legacy Basic"
   Expected: "your plan".
5. entitlement.display_name = empty string; workspace.plan_name = "Legacy Basic"
   Expected: "your plan".
6. entitlement.display_name = whitespace-only; workspace.plan_name = "Legacy Basic"
   Expected: "your plan".

Template acceptance criteria
- Renewal reminder passes every matrix case.
- Trial-expiry education passes every matrix case; no blank phrase is permitted.
- Integration summary passes every matrix case.
- Rendered output contains no workspace.plan_name-derived value and no literal template error or blank entitlement phrase.
- The full-workspace/template scan confirms no active reference to workspace.plan_name in the three production paths, including shared snippets and conditional branches.
- Existing audience, trigger, eligibility, suppression, routing, links, and state-writing behavior are unchanged; record any unrelated diff as a release blocker.

Evidence and disposition
Retain one rendered preview per matrix case per template, the template/version identifier, source-field inspection, and the scan result. Any failure is REJECTED and the affected template/send path remains held until corrected and rerun; do not substitute workspace.plan_name as a workaround.
